column1: # startup-touch executed-page symbol coverage -- 2026-09-01 seat07 -- row rtx-startup-touch-rewrites, ## NEXT item 1
# THE DERIVATION THE ITEM CALLS "THE RUNG": the full startup-executed function list + the page span that
#   sizes the linker-ordering lever. Supersedes the top-15 EXCERPT in FINDING-2026-08-28-seat03; that
#   FINDING named 15 of them and estimated 65, this is the whole set, re-derived.
# instrument: valgrind --tool=callgrind --collect-atstart=yes  (⛔ perf is NON-FUNCTIONAL in this container:
#   /usr/bin/perf exists and linux-tools reports Installed, but the package ships no perf binary for
#   6.17.0-1032-oem; perf record exits 2. Same substitution seat03 made and for the same reason.)
#   x  nm -SC --defined-only  on the linked .so AND on each out/rt_pic-*/*.o for source attribution.
#   SCRIP 14f384ed, RT_OPT=-O0 (NO -O2 BUILDS), make pristine, mode 3 (--run).
# ⛔ TWO PARSING TRAPS, both hit and both cured here -- a hand-rolled reader gets a PLAUSIBLE WRONG LIST:
#   (1) callgrind name compression: the spec says "a separate ID mapping for each position specification",
#       but its OWN example defines ID 2 via `cfn=(2) func1` and resolves it via `fn=(2)`. The namespace is
#       per ENTITY KIND (file/function/object), not per keyword. Keying by keyword drops every definition a
#       call-side spec made: measured 741 of 753 rows came back object='???' before the fix, 0 after.
#   (2) callgrind DEMANGLES C++ and nm does not (nm -C), and it appends a recursion-context suffix (fn'2)
#       that is the SAME function. Unfixed, both inflate the "unresolved" bucket and undercount the list.
# METRIC NOTE (hq_P's standing direction + seat01's 2026-09-01 lesson): pages-spanned is a STRUCTURAL metric
#   and an UPPER BOUND -- Linux fault-around maps up to 16 pages per fault, and a function executing does not
#   mean all its bytes were. The graded metric stays faults/RSS. Do not quote a page delta as a fault delta.
# measured m3 do-nothing floor, this tree, 5 runs: minflt 743,744,744,744,743  maxrss 8976-9104 kB
